header.title: BIM Validator
header.heroAlt: BIM Validator with an office model in 3D: the external wall without a U-value is highlighted, on the right the result per requirement of the NL-BIM Basis ILS
header.label: BIM checking
header.tagline: Know before handover whether your IFC model meets the requirements
header.desc: Add an IFC model in the browser, choose the NL-BIM Basis ILS, the RVB BIM Norm or your own IDS file and click Validate. You see per requirement what passes and fails, and every failing element lights up in 3D.

meta.description: Free, open-source checking of IFC models against IDS requirements, with the Dutch NL-BIM Basis ILS and RVB BIM Norm built in. See every error in 3D and pass it on as a BCF issue. Runs in the browser on your own server.
meta.title: BIM Validator — OpenAEC Foundation

deur.alt: A door with a non-standard name highlighted in 3D; on the right the door naming requirement with the failing element and its details
deur.title: See straight away which element is wrong
deur.desc: Click an error in the results and the app zooms to the element while the rest of the model turns transparent. Next to it you see the requirement, type, GlobalId and name, so you can find it quickly in your own BIM software.

standaarden.alt: Result of the RVB BIM Norm: 26 requirements, ten of them met, with the office model in 3D
standaarden.title: The Dutch requirements are built in
standaarden.desc: Choose the NL-BIM Basis ILS (12 requirements) or the RVB BIM Norm of the Dutch Government Real Estate Agency (26 requirements) with one click: naming, NL/SfB codes, materials, fire resistance, U-values and more. Does your client have their own requirements? Load their IDS file.

eigenschappen.alt: A window selected in the 3D model; on the left its properties with storey, material and NL/SfB code
eigenschappen.title: Click an element and see what is in it
eigenschappen.desc: Orbit, zoom and click through the model without installing anything. For each element you see the storey, material, classification, property sets and quantities. Section planes let you look inside the building.

bcf.alt: Six BCF issues with thumbnails, created from the failed requirements, and the button to download them as a BCF zip
bcf.title: Pass the errors on to the modeller
bcf.desc: Turn all errors into BCF issues with one click, with your own prefix, priority, assignee and deadline. Each issue gets a viewpoint and a thumbnail. Download them as a BCF zip for Revit, ArchiCAD, Solibri or BIMcollab, or push them to the OpenAEC BCF platform.

notice.text: No release and no public web version yet: you set it up on a server yourself with Docker. The screenshots come from a local test setup with a fictitious model.

whatsnew.label: New in April 2026
whatsnew.title: Projects, saving and section planes
whatsnew.desc: The latest new features date from April 2026. There is no release yet; the changes are in the source code on GitHub.

files.a: IFC models in IFC2X3 and IFC4, as exported from Revit, ArchiCAD, Tekla or other BIM software, up to 500 MB per file. Requirements are loaded as an IDS file (up to 5 MB).

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: Users don't: they work in the browser. Someone does need to set up the validator once on a server with Docker. There is no ready-made release and no public trial version yet.

price.a: Nothing. BIM Validator is open source under the MIT licence. You only pay for your own server.

save.q: In which file format is my work saved?
save.a: A project keeps your IFC models, the results and the issues together, with a project file (.wefc) that records what belongs with what. Issues download as a BCF 2.1 zip, results as JSON; from the command line also as an HTML report.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Users need a modern browser with WebGL, on Windows, macOS or Linux. The server runs in Docker on Linux. There is no desktop app.

practice.a: Yes. The Dutch NL-BIM Basis ILS and RVB BIM Norm v1.1 are built in, with NL/SfB classification. Requirements follow the buildingSMART IDS standard, issues the BCF 2.1 standard that Revit, ArchiCAD, Solibri and BIMcollab read.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: Through the REST API an assistant or script can have a model checked and fetch the results as JSON; the command line works too. There is no MCP server yet.

privacy.q: Do my models stay inside my organisation?
privacy.a: Yes. You run the validator on your own server, so models don't go to an external service. With several organisations on one server, each organisation only sees its own projects.

clash.q: Can it also find clashes between models?
clash.a: Not yet. The Clashes tab is already there, but clash detection has not been built yet. You can view several models together.

ifcos.desc: The check itself: IfcTester tests the model against the IDS requirements, IfcOpenShell reads the IFC file.

fastapi.desc: The server with the REST API, background checks and the ifc-validate command line.

thatopen.desc: The 3D viewer in the browser, with fragments for fast display of large models.

react.desc: The interface with ribbon, panels and themes, in Dutch and English.

storage.desc: Projects in PostgreSQL (SQLite for local testing) and files in Nextcloud via WebDAV.

docker.desc: A single Docker Compose setup with optional sign-in via OpenID Connect.
